one_liner: Cloud team chat (channels, DMs, files, calls) with a free workspace, an HTTP API via API keys and OAuth2 app tokens, and a vendor-hosted MCP server at mcp.pumble.com.

auth.notes: The integration path the SDK documents for an app acting for workspace users is OAuth2 (consent screen, then an access token and bot token). A simpler per-user API key exists via the API addon, and creating an app in the workspace also yields static app key, user token, and bot token sent as request headers (the scheme the official MCP server uses).

access.notes: Cloud only. Anyone can open a free workspace (owner of that workspace). The API addon and custom-app credentials are documented as available on all plans, and a free workspace may install up to 3 addons. Only owners and admins can install apps, so a member in someone else’s workspace may be blocked unless an admin installs the addon or turns off the optional “request app approval” setting. Marketplace listing review was not verified.

api.notes: There is a documented HTTP API, not SDK-only. The API-key addon covers sending and replying to messages, reactions, deletion, channel creation, and listing channels and messages. The OAuth/app-token client covers messages (including search, threads, scheduled messages, drafts), channels, users, workspace info, calls, and files, with read and write scopes. Incoming webhooks are HTTP POST. Help articles and the SDK reference are readable without login. The vendor also points at https://docs.pumble.com, which did not render here.

mcp.notes: Hosted by Pumble at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp. Auth is the app key (x-app-token) plus a user or bot token. Tools depend on selected scopes and include messages, channels, users, reactions, files, calls, and search. Third-party servers also exist (for example shoutkol/pumble-mcp-server); the official one is usable now and is not described as beta.

verdict.rationale: A developer can create a free Pumble workspace, install the API addon (documented as available on all plans, with up to three addons on Free) or create an app, and call a public HTTP API for messages, channels, and users with an API key or OAuth2/user and bot tokens. Pumble also hosts a generally available MCP server for those same credentials.
